A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same time-to-inconsistency study. Their text, equations, tables, figure, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original survival-model evaluations, calibration results, proportional-hazards tests, and drift-effect analyses using MT-Consistency conversations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical analyses and additionally reports AFT feature-effect comparisons and an evaluated retrospective risk monitor.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2-3.3 replace averaged prior-prompt embeddings with an embedding of concatenated dialogue history for context drift, omit the baseline Cox gamma-frailty term, and remove prompt length from the model-interaction block. Section 5.5 adds a conditional-failure-probability monitor with thresholded alerts, whereas v1 only proposed monitoring as an application. These are changes to the reported procedure; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use MT-Consistency with 700 questions, 39 subjects grouped into seven domains, four difficulty bands, nine LLMs, eight attack templates, and an eight-turn horizon. The new monitoring evaluation uses the same conversation setting and inconsistency outcome; the expanded model list documents retained coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains two Cox variants, six AFT variants, and RSF, although Cox specifications are revised. V2 Table 4 adds an actually evaluated drift-threshold baseline for the new monitoring comparison; no such comparison appears in v1.

E3.justification: V1 specifies AIC/BIC selection for Cox/AFT and out-of-bag scoring for RSF; v2 specifies fivefold training-pool cross-validation using IBS, with a C-index tie-breaker for Cox. The 80/20 conversation split remains. The new monitoring protocol evaluates a two-turn warning horizon, a training-F1-selected threshold, alert frequency, and lead time on 140 conversations, including 88 failures and 52 censored cases.

E4.justification: V1 Figure 1 reports Cox hazard ratios alone. V2 Section 5.3 and Figure 1 add AFT acceleration factors across the same drift features and displayed LLMs to test whether the central feature interpretations withstand the proportional-hazards violation. The existing Schoenfeld analysis is retained in Appendix D, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Conversation-clustered standard errors and Schoenfeld/log-rank testing are retained, with unchanged reported p-values. Appendix D explains the existing grouped diagnostics more fully. Neither version reports repeated-run variability or confidence intervals for predictive scores; the new cross-validation protocol concerns tuning rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds AFT effect estimates, including GPT-4o prompt-to-prompt AF approximately 0.15 and cumulative-drift time factors of 1.4-2.6. Its new monitor alerts 76% of failing conversations versus 62% for the drift baseline, alerts 19% of censored conversations versus 32%, and provides a median two-turn warning. The original performance, roundwise Brier, PH-test, and risk-stratification table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Local formal changes include the context-drift definition, removal of the gamma-frailty assumption, and the new monitoring quantity Risk(t, tau) = 1 - S(t + tau)/S(t). The discrete survival-hazard relationship and three AFT distribution families remain; their standard formulas are condensed into Appendix A. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: V1 presents monitoring as a potential application and claims the first comprehensive/systematic survival analysis of this problem. V2 removes that explicit firstness claim and makes demonstrated early warning with modest false alerts a central contribution in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The principal drift-direction and AFT-performance claims are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations covering the single benchmark, eight-turn horizon, binary failure labeling, single embedding model, and retrospective monitoring without interventions or user outcomes. It also treats Cox effects as descriptive under PH violations and interprets Cox-AFT agreement as stronger evidence for adaptation than v1's tentative adaptation or pressure-decay explanation.

D1.justification: V2 names all nine evaluated LLMs and documents pooling, split stratification, and AFT conversation summaries. Appendix E newly supplies tuning grids and selected penalties, plus RSF settings of 500 trees, maximum depth 8, and mtry 7. V1's explicit numerical-stability reparameterization is omitted, but implementation documentation expands substantially.

R1.justification: V2 adds Ishwaran et al. (2008) and removes citations to Dubois, Ganguli, Morris, Perez, and Wang et al. Section 2.3 more explicitly distinguishes prior dialogue/session-outcome modeling from adversarial LLM inconsistency, while the broader related-work coverage remains largely intact.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, methods, experimental setup, and discussion, including an explicit three-part contribution list and limitations discussion. It reorganizes the results narrative and moves condensed AFT mathematics and PH diagnostics into expanded appendices.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned from Cox-only bars into paired solid Cox and hatched AFT bars, with revised axes, legends, and caption. V2 adds the monitoring comparison table and hyperparameter-grid table, and moves v1's main-text PH table to Appendix D as Table 7. The benchmark-score and subject/prompt tables retain their substantive contents.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through named models, explicit tuning grids, and concrete limitations, and strengthens the previously Cox-only drift analysis with an AFT cross-check. The offline monitor supplies evidence for an application that v1 only proposed. These gains are limited by unresolved links between revised method specifications and unchanged main tables, and by unclear selection of the monitor's 140 conversations and timing of its AFT covariate summaries. The additions support a modest quality improvement without establishing intervention effectiveness or the stronger adaptation interpretation.
